problem_text:
A city is devising a strategy to curtail digital noise pollution emanating from a network of major data hubs. Presently, no mitigation protocols are in place.

The profile for each data hub is characterized by its inherent noise emission coefficient and its operational data throughput:
*   Hub Alpha has an emission coefficient of 2.922 and a throughput of 222.125.
*   Hub Beta has an emission coefficient of 2.234 and a throughput of 81.837.
*   Hub Gamma has an emission coefficient of 2.822 and a throughput of 232.208.
*   Hub Delta has an emission coefficient of 2.467 and a throughput of 287.197.
*   Hub Epsilon has an emission coefficient of 1.058 and a throughput of 287.175.
*   Hub Zeta has an emission coefficient of 1.972 and a throughput of 147.9.
*   Hub Eta has an emission coefficient of 0.938 and a throughput of 298.571.
*   Hub Theta has an emission coefficient of 1.267 and a throughput of 291.296.

To suppress this digital noise, a suite of filtering algorithms can be deployed, each with a distinct suppression rate:
*   Algorithm A achieves an 87% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm B achieves a 42% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm C achieves a 16% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm D achieves a 13% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm E achieves a 72% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm F achieves a 45% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm G achieves a 15% noise reduction.
*   Algorithm H achieves a 79% noise reduction.

Implementing a filtering algorithm at a hub incurs a computational cost per unit of data throughput. The cost matrix for all hub-algorithm pairings is provided:

| Hub \ Algorithm | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alpha | 151.615 | 55.219 | 196.652 | 41.899 | 178.211 | 26.858 | 144.704 | 131.43 |
| Beta | 178.464 | 94.86 | 60.39 | 57.413 | 22.881 | 58.765 | 30.527 | 10.243 |
| Gamma | 83.328 | 149.191 | 194.129 | 178.065 | 103.686 | 81.955 | 113.745 | 29.271 |
| Delta | 101.103 | 174.17 | 133.684 | 140.56 | 40.905 | 24.005 | 170.695 | 66.033 |
| Epsilon | 70.556 | 190.816 | 24.098 | 42.32 | 81.337 | 149.077 | 113.939 | 180.644 |
| Zeta | 27.69 | 122.866 | 126.592 | 101.72 | 15.889 | 189.064 | 41.349 | 179.053 |
| Eta | 39.85 | 29.239 | 49.055 | 46.097 | 142.467 | 147.187 | 148.695 | 60.4 |
| Theta | 63.489 | 55.134 | 19.431 | 118.636 | 169.572 | 39.182 | 78.557 | 91.245 |

The task is to determine which filtering algorithms to apply to each hub (hubs may employ multiple algorithms concurrently), and it is permissible for a hub to operate with only partial noise suppression. The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate digital noise is diminished by at least a target fraction \( P = 0.347 \) of the baseline level \( E_0 \), while minimizing the total computational expenditure.
